ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. Single-model baselines are around 0.80-0.82 AUROC, with H-optimus-1 the best at 0.824. Metadata alone is weak (0.60) but adds a little to UNI2-h and Virchow2. Fold SDs of about 0.04-0.05 mean only a gain of roughly 0.01 or more is likely to be accepted.
REASONING: Start with a robust, low-variance fusion baseline: late fusion with mean_prob. It averages three per-model logistic regressions, which typically reduces variance when the models make partly independent errors. C=0.01 on standardised high-dimensional features is a reasonable strong-regularisation default for 134 training patients. I will skip L2 norm and PCA for now to keep the anchor simple. meta_weight=1 is the default.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.83-0.84, above the best single model, giving an accepted anchor. If it comes in at or below 0.82, the models' errors are highly correlated or C is mis-set. Next I would vary C (0.001 or 0.1) or try early fusion with balance_blocks.

ANALYSIS: Late fusion with mean_prob at C=0.01 gives 0.8298, only slightly above the best single model (hoptimus1 0.8236), so this gain is likely within noise. Lepidic and Papillary are the weakest classes. Early fusion is untested, and so is the effect of C under fusion.
REASONING: Early fusion with balance_blocks is the main untested method. It lets one linear model use complementary features across the three models. With about 5600 dims and 134 patients, strong regularisation is needed. C=0.01 on standardised features matched the late setting, but the concatenation is wider, so C=0.001 is a sensible choice. balance_blocks=True keeps Virchow2's larger block from dominating.
EXPECTED: AUROC of about 0.83-0.84 if cross-model feature interactions help Lepidic or Papillary. If early fusion lands at or below 0.83, the models are largely redundant at slide level and the gains must come from ensembling (late), so I would next tune the late fusion's C and combine method.

ANALYSIS: Late mean_prob fusion (0.830) and early balanced concatenation (0.829) are essentially tied and only modestly above the best single model, H-optimus-1 at 0.824. Lepidic (0.75) and Papillary (0.73) are the weak classes. Regularisation strength (C) and per-slide L2 normalisation have not been explored for late fusion, and the stack combiner and gated method are still untested.
REASONING: Before adding fusion complexity, I want to check whether the base learners are badly regularised. C=0.01 on raw 1536- to 2560-d standardised features may be either too strong or too weak. Per-slide L2 normalisation often helps mean-pooled foundation-model embeddings. I will change one sensible pair: keep late mean_prob, turn on L2 normalisation, and loosen C to 0.1. This tests a plausible clear gain without consuming budget on combiner variants.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.835-0.845 if the base models were over-shrunk, with Lepidic and Papillary improving. If AUROC drops or stays flat, C=0.01 is near optimal for late fusion. In that case I would try C=0.001 to test the other direction and then move to the stack or learned_weights combiners.

ANALYSIS: Late mean_prob fusion (0.830) only modestly beats the best single model (H-optimus-1 0.824). Early fusion with balance_blocks performs the same, so the fusion method matters little at this C. L2 normalisation plus higher C hurt (-0.011), which suggests that weaker regularisation or the L2 step is harmful. The weak classes are Papillary and Lepidic.
REASONING: Regularisation strength is the most influential knob still untested for late fusion. C=0.01 may be too strong or too weak. With n=134 and 1.5k-2.5k dimensions, strong shrinkage usually works best, so C=0.001 is worth testing. Stronger shrinkage also smooths the base probabilities, which tends to help mean_prob AUROC. Everything else stays as in #1, so the C effect is isolated.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC of about 0.83-0.84, with a possible gain on Papillary and Lepidic. If it is no better or worse, the C optimum lies at or above 0.01, and I will next probe C=0.1 without L2, or change the combiner (mean_logit or stack) instead.

ANALYSIS: Late mean_prob fusion at C=0.01 (0.830) is the best so far, about 0.006 above the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.824). Early fusion at C=0.001 is essentially tied with it. Moving C to 0.001 hurt, and L2 normalisation combined with C=0.1 hurt, so the linear-fusion knobs near this point look saturated. Lepidic (~0.74) and Papillary (~0.72) are the weak classes in every trial.
REASONING: Small C and combine tweaks on late or early fusion will probably give gains below the ~0.005-0.009 threshold. The gated method is completely untested, and it is the only option that can weight models per patient, which could help the confusable Lepidic and Papillary slides. I chose a heavily regularised setting for 134 training patients: PCA 64 per model to cut input dimension, hidden 32, dropout 0.5, weight_decay 0.1, 200 epochs at lr 1e-3, and 3 seeds averaged to reduce variance.
EXPECTED: If gating helps, AUROC should reach about 0.835-0.845, with Lepidic and Papillary improving. If it scores at or below about 0.82 with high fold SD, I will conclude it overfits at this sample size and return to linear fusion: late with stack or learned_weights, and PCA with a larger C.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at about 0.82–0.83 AUROC, only slightly above H-optimus-1 alone (0.824). Late mean_prob at C=0.01 is the best so far (0.8298). Early fusion on the raw concatenation (C=0.001) ties with it. L2 normalisation, a smaller C and the gated network all hurt or did nothing. Lepidic (~0.74) and Papillary (~0.72) are the weak classes in every trial.
REASONING: The open structural question is whether early fusion is limited by dimensionality: about 5.6k raw columns against 134 patients per fold. PCA to 32 components per model leaves about 96 dense features, so a weaker penalty (C=0.01) can let the model learn interactions across the three models. balance_blocks stays on, as in the early tie, so each model gets equal weight. Untested PCA in early fusion is the change most likely to move the score clearly, rather than another small C tweak on late fusion.
EXPECTED: If compression helps, AUROC should reach about 0.84 or more, with gains on Lepidic and Papillary that pass the roughly 0.005–0.01 threshold. If it scores about the same or lower, PCA discards the discriminative variance and raw high-dimensional features with strong shrinkage are better. I would then go back to late fusion and test stack or learned_weights, and meta_weight=3.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants cluster at 0.82-0.83, only ~0.006 above the best single model (hoptimus1). L2 norm hurt late fusion, and C=0.001 was slightly worse than C=0.01 for late. Early, gated and PCA variants are all within noise of trial #1. Lepidic and Papillary (~0.73-0.75) are the weak classes everywhere.
REASONING: The combiner in late fusion is untested; mean_prob weights all models equally. A stacker on base log-probabilities can learn class-specific reweighting across models, for example trusting the model that best separates Papillary or Lepidic, and it is the knob most likely to move per-class AUROC. Keeping C=0.01 (the best base) isolates the effect of the combiner. stack_C=0.1 gives moderate regularisation for 21 features on about 107 inner-CV predictions.
EXPECTED: If model complementarity is class-specific, AUROC should rise to about 0.84+, with gains in Papi/Lepi. If it is flat or worse, the three models are largely redundant (the stacker only adds variance), and I would next try mean_logit or a higher meta_weight rather than more complex combiners.

ANALYSIS: All fusions cluster at 0.82-0.83, only marginally above the best single model (H-optimus-1 at 0.824). Late mean_prob with C=0.01 is the best so far. Moving C away from 0.01 in either direction hurt, as did L2 normalisation. Stacking lost ground (0.816), which fits the small training set making a second-level learner noisy. Early fusion with balanced blocks ties the best. Metadata adds little alone, though meta_weight has never been varied above 1.
REASONING: The cheap, untested question is metadata weighting. Age and sex lifted Virchow2 and UNI2-h by about 0.01 as single models. Within the late scheme each base model gets age/sex, so raising meta_weight to 3 lets the metadata signal escape the strong shrinkage at C=0.01. That shrinkage likely suppresses it now. Everything else stays at the best config (late, C=0.01, mean_prob), so the effect is isolated.
EXPECTED: I expect a gain of about 0.005-0.01, possibly enough to clear the ~0.005-0.009 threshold. If it does not help, metadata is not limited by shrinkage. I would then stop exploring meta_weight and test mean_logit or learned_weights, or PCA within late fusion.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants land at about 0.82–0.83 AUROC, roughly 0.006 above the best single model (hoptimus1, 0.8236), and none beat trial #1. In late fusion, raising C from 0.001 (#4) to 0.01 (#1) gained about 0.0075. C=0.1 was only tried together with L2 normalisation (#3), which hurt, so the two effects are confounded. Stacking, gating, metadata weighting and PCA added nothing beyond noise.
REASONING: The most informative open question with a plausible clear gain is whether the C trend keeps going once L2 normalisation is removed. This trial isolates C=0.1 under the same settings as #1. The more flexible combiners (stack, gated) overfit with 134 training patients, so tuning the base learners' regularisation is a better bet than adding combiner complexity.
EXPECTED: If weaker regularisation helps, AUROC should reach about 0.835–0.84 and could clear the roughly 0.005–0.009 threshold. If it scores at or below 0.83, the C optimum is near 0.01 and the fusion ceiling is about 0.83. I would then try only low-variance combiners (mean_logit or learned_weights) before stopping.

ANALYSIS: Fusion gives a small but consistent lift over the best single model: late mean_prob at C=0.01 scores 0.830, against 0.824 for H-optimus alone. Early fusion (#2, #6) matches it. Changing C (0.001 or 0.1), L2 normalisation, meta_weight and stacking all lowered AUROC or left it unchanged. The one gated trial was noisier, with no clear gain. Per-class weak points are Lepidic and Papillary (about 0.72-0.77), and no variant has moved them.
REASONING: The main untested lever in the best family is how the three model probabilities are combined. Equal-weight mean_prob may underweight H-optimus, the strongest model. learned_weights, fitted by inner CV, has only 2 free parameters, so it is much less prone to overfitting than stacking (#7). Keeping C=0.01 and the other settings from #1 means any difference comes from the combiner alone.
EXPECTED: I expect a modest gain of about +0.003 to +0.008, mostly on classes where H-optimus is strongest, which may or may not clear the threshold. If it is flat or worse, equal weighting is already near-optimal and the late combiner space is exhausted. I would then try one more strongly regularised gated variant or PCA within late fusion, and stop otherwise.

ANALYSIS: All fusions cluster at 0.82-0.83 AUROC, with late mean_prob at C=0.01 (0.8298) the best so far. That is about +0.006 over the best single model. C=0.01 is clearly optimal for late fusion: both 0.001 and 0.1 lose about 0.008-0.010. L2 normalisation hurt, and stacking, learned weights, gated fusion and higher meta_weight added nothing. Weak classes (Papillary 0.72, Lepidic 0.74) are stable across methods, which suggests a shared limit in the embeddings rather than in the fusion.
REASONING: Six trials remain before the stop. The main untested axis for late fusion is per-model PCA. Projecting each roughly 1500-2500-d embedding onto its top 32 components inside the fold acts as stronger spectral regularisation than L2 alone. That could stabilise each base model on 134 patients and lift the weak classes. In early fusion, PCA=32 scored about the same as no PCA (0.8279 vs 0.8290), so the effect is uncertain. Testing it on the best method, while keeping the proven C=0.01 and mean_prob, isolates that question.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC between 0.825 and 0.835, with a possible small gain on Lepidic and Papillary. If it is not accepted, dimensionality reduction does not help either fusion family. I would then conclude the space is near its ceiling of about 0.83, keep trial #1, and spend at most one or two of the remaining trials on mean_logit or a heavily regularised gated model before the search stops.

ANALYSIS: Fusion sits at about 0.83 AUROC. Late mean_prob (C=0.01), early fusion, PCA, meta_weight, stacking and learned weights all land within noise of each other or below it. C=0.01 is the sweet spot for late fusion, and L2 norm and stacking hurt. The one method with a clearly different per-class profile is gated #5 (Crib 0.86, Micr 0.88, but weaker Acinar and In situ). It overfit, though: lower mean AUROC and the highest fold SD.
REASONING: With 5 non-improving trials left before the search stops, small tweaks to late or early fusion (mean_logit, weighted_vote, meta_weight=10) are unlikely to clear a threshold of about 0.005-0.01. The only plausible route to a clear gain is a model that captures complementary signal. Gated already shows complementary per-class strengths but is under-regularised. This trial tests a much more constrained gate: PCA 32, hidden 16, weight decay 1.0, dropout 0.5, and 100 epochs. That should cut variance while keeping per-patient model weighting.
EXPECTED: If regularisation was the issue, I expect gated to reach about 0.83-0.84 with Crib and Micr kept high and Acinar and In situ recovered, and a lower fold SD. If it stays at or below about 0.825, I will conclude the gate adds variance without usable signal. In that case fusion has plateaued near 0.83, and late mean_prob C=0.01 (+0.006 over the best single model) stands as the final answer.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants land at 0.815-0.830 AUROC, against 0.824 for the best single model (H-optimus-1), so fusion gains so far are tiny. Late mean_prob at C=0.01 is best. Stronger or weaker C, L2 norm, stacking, learned weights and both gated configs were all equal or worse. Per-class patterns are stable: Papillary (~0.72) and Lepidic (~0.74) are the weak classes. PCA32 helps Lepidic but hurts Cribriform.
REASONING: Early fusion with balanced blocks was within 0.001 of the best at C=0.001 without PCA. It was only tried at C=0.01 together with PCA32. Block balancing scales each block down by 1/sqrt(columns), which makes the effective penalty much stronger. So C=0.001 on the full features is probably over-regularised, and C=0.01 on the full balanced features is the untested cell most likely to beat late mean_prob. It also settles whether the PCA or the C value drove #6.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.83-0.84, with BA staying around 0.45, the higher level seen in the early-fusion trials. If it does not clear the threshold, early and late fusion are both capped near 0.83. I would then conclude the three foundation models carry largely redundant slide-level information and that the remaining trials will not yield a robust gain.

ANALYSIS: Fusion is stuck at about 0.83 AUROC, only about 0.006 above the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8236). Late mean_prob at C=0.01 is a sharp optimum: C=0.1 and C=0.001 both lose. Stacking, learned weights, PCA and gated variants all fall short of the threshold. Early fusion with balanced blocks did better at C=0.001 (0.8290) than at C=0.01 (0.8240), so stronger regularisation helps early fusion, and that trend has not yet been tested further.
REASONING: With 3 non-improving trials left before the stop, the trial should test the one open trend in the log rather than another combiner variant that is likely within noise. Early fusion has the most features (about 5.6k) and so the most to gain from heavy shrinkage. The step from C=0.01 to C=0.001 gained 0.005, so testing C=0.0001 tells us whether early fusion keeps improving or has peaked. Block balancing stays on, and there is no PCA, L2 norm or metadata upweighting, because none of those helped.
EXPECTED: If shrinkage keeps helping, AUROC should reach about 0.833-0.838, which could pass the threshold of about 0.005. If it drops or stays flat, early fusion peaks near C=0.001. I would then conclude that the three models carry largely redundant slide-level signal, so fusion gives at most about +0.006 over H-optimus-1, and trial #1 stays the best.

ANALYSIS: Linear fusions plateau at about 0.823-0.830 AUROC. The best is late mean_prob at C=0.01 (0.8298), only about 0.006 above H-optimus-1 alone. Changes to C, PCA, meta_weight, L2 norm, stacking and learned weights all gave gains of zero or less. The per-class profiles are nearly identical across linear variants. Gated trial #5 was the exception: it had the best Cribriform (0.86) and Micropapillary (0.88) scores but weaker Acinar and In situ.
REASONING: With 2 trials left before the stop rule, another small linear tweak (for example mean_logit versus mean_prob) is very unlikely to clear a threshold of about 0.005. The only family with a qualitatively different error profile is gated. Trial #12, which regularised more heavily than #5, was worse, so the direction to test is the opposite: more capacity and less regularisation. This trial uses a wider hidden layer, moderate dropout, lighter weight decay and fewer epochs to limit overfitting, keeping PCA at 64 as in #5. It is a higher-variance trial with real upside, and it answers whether the gate can be tuned rather than only shrunk.
EXPECTED: If the gate adds per-patient model selection, I expect AUROC of about 0.83-0.84 that keeps #5's Cribriform and Micropapillary gains while recovering Acinar. If it lands at or below 0.824, the gated family offers no gain at this sample size. Taken with the linear plateau, I would then conclude that fusion gives at most a marginal, statistically unresolved gain over H-optimus-1, and that late mean_prob at C=0.01 is the defensible final choice.

ANALYSIS: All 15 fusion trials cluster at 0.80-0.83 AUROC, and none beat late mean_prob at C=0.01 (0.8298). The best fusion is only about 0.006 above the strongest single model (hoptimus1, 0.8236). Stronger or weaker regularisation, L2 norm, PCA, stacking, learned weights and gating all failed to help or hurt. Per-class AUROCs barely move across configurations, with Papillary and Lepidic as the persistent weak classes, so performance looks limited by the data rather than by how the models are fused.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the 15-in-a-row stop, so it should answer the one clean open question left in the most promising region. mean_logit (geometric mean of probabilities) is the only untested low-variance combiner. I keep it at the best base setting (C=0.01, no PCA, no L2 norm, meta_weight=1). It adds no fitted parameters, unlike stack and learned_weights, which both lost, probably from inner-CV noise with about 107 inner patients. Logit averaging rewards agreement between models more sharply than probability averaging, which could help the minority classes.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.828-0.833, a change within ±0.005 of trial #1, most likely below the acceptance threshold. If it is not accepted, the search ends. My conclusion would be that simple late averaging at C=0.01 is the robust fusion choice and that its gain over H-optimus-1 alone is small (about 0.006 AUROC). That difference should be confirmed on the locked test set rather than claimed from CV.
